messages:
aaron-ml: Heads up — during onboarding for hawthorn-14b I noticed a non-standard clause in the LICENSE that might affect how we can serve / redistribute quantized artifacts. Can legal weigh in?

aaron-ml: snippet from LICENSE.txt:```
2. Restrictions:
   - Model weights and derivative binaries may be used for internal inference only.
   - Hosting the model as a service for third-party customers is permitted only with written vendor approval.
   - Export of the model or derivatives is subject to applicable export controls; US/EU restrictions may apply.
```

melissa-eng: @sarah-legal cc: we plan to run quant experiments (4-bit) and potentially expose the model behind Redwood Dedicated / Private. Questions: is hosting behind our API considered "hosting as a service for third-party customers"? And does producing quantized binaries count as "derivative binaries" under this clause?

devon-infra: also: if we allow Dedicated customers to pin this model in their private pools, are we considered redistributing? The customer gets inference endpoint only, no weights.

legal-bot: Created ticket LEG-2024-338 — assigning to @sarah-legal for review. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/LEG-2024-338 :white_check_mark:

sarah-legal: Quick read — thanks for flagging. Short answers for triage: 1) "Derivative binaries" is often interpreted to include any transformed weight artifacts (e.g., quantized checkpoints) unless the license explicitly exempts them. 2) "Hosting as a service" language varies: some vendors mean public multi-tenant hosting; others include managed hosting for customers. We need to confirm vendor intent. 3) Export control clause means we should check model provenance (training data/location / upstream restrictions) and whether vendor is in control list.

sarah-legal: Concrete next steps: (a) I will ask the vendor (contact in onboarding pack) to confirm whether quantized checkpoints are considered "derivative binaries" and whether written approval can be scoped to hosting behind an API (hosted + dedicated) without providing weights. (b) We'll request an explicit carve-out that allows serving via Redwood Hosted/Dedicated and Private (VPC) where customers do not receive raw weights. (c) If they refuse, we likely can still run internal evals and hosted inference for internal use but cannot enable Dedicated/customer-facing endpoints without a signed exception.

melissa-eng: For implementation: if legal requires an exception we can gate rollout behind a config flag and disable model publish to Dedicated until approval. Good to know the safe default is internal-only.

devon-infra: Noted — we'll add a model gating check in the catalog import pipeline and set hawthorn-14b to quarantine state until LEG sign-off.

sarah-legal: Also important: attribution requirements. Does LICENSE demand attribution in product UI or docs? If yes, we need to capture exact wording to implement compliance (toast/footnote in console or endpoint headers). Ask vendor for required attribution text and placement.

aaron-ml: Got it. I'll update the onboarding PR with quarantine flag and attach the LEG ticket. I'll ping vendor now for clarifications and post their response here.

legal-bot: LEG-2024-338 updated: vendor reply requested.

aaron-ml: (later) vendor replied: they say quantized checkpoints are "derivative binaries" and require a redistribution/hosting approval. They provided a template approval form and a suggested attribution line: "Model: Hawthorn-14B (research license)." They also asked we don't export weights outside jurisdictions listed in their export appendix. Copy of their reply attached to LEG ticket.

sarah-legal: Thanks — I'll review the template approval. Initial take: we can negotiate an approval that permits serving via Hosted & Dedicated (no weights to customers) and allows Private deployments where customer-managed infra prevents us from sharing weights. We will also need to add a compliance check to ensure we don't enable weight export for these models.

melissa-eng: OK to proceed with internal evals and benchmarking in quarantine. We'll run quant experiments but won't push quant artifacts to public buckets; keep them behind KMS and mark as restricted.

devon-infra: I'll add automated guardrails: 1) block any S3 bucket lifecycle that marks these artifacts as publicly accessible, 2) deny export to external registries, 3) require an explicit LEG sign-off tag to flip model.status=approved.

aaron-ml: Thanks everyone — holding onboarding until LEG sign-off and vendor-signed approval. Will update ticket with experiment notes and the attribution string so legal can finalize the wording. :thumbsup:
